records.failureSummary: Implemented src/csv.mjs exporting parseCsvLine(line) for the slice-1 subset, and confirmed it is the only changed file. Behavior: returns [] when typeof line !== 'string' (covers null, undefined, number, boolean, object, array, symbol with no exception) (FR-6); returns [] for the empty string (FR-4); otherwise a single-pass character scan splits on the comma only, preserving each field's leading/trailing whitespace verbatim with no trim (FR-1); the final field is always pushed so a trailing comma yields a trailing empty string (FR-5). No quoted-field logic (FR-2/FR-3) was added, no dependencies were introduced, and no build or lint configuration was changed. All eight listed acceptance criteria were verified directly against the module: 'a,b,c' to ['a','b','c']; ' a , b ' to [' a ',' b ']; 'a, b' to ['a',' b']; '' to []; 'a,' to ['a','']; ',a' to ['','a']; ',,' to ['','','']; and null/undefined/123/{}/[]/true/symbol each to [] without throwing. npm run build (node --check src/csv.mjs) exits 0 and npm run lint (node --check src/csv.mjs) exits 0. npm run test reports 2 passed / 1 failed, where the single failure is the seed test test/csv.test.mjs line 10 asserting FR-2 quoted-field behavior (parseCsvLine('a,"b,c",d')), which is explicitly out of scope for this slice and was flagged as a scope conflict by the T-2 design and the prior attempt. src/csv.mjs is the only modified file (git status: ' M src/csv.mjs').
